subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the term for a couple living together in a sexual relationship without being married?
questions.explain: Cohabitation is when a couple live together, and usually have a sexual relationship, without being married.

questions.q: In the Catholic Church, marriage is regarded as a...
questions.explain: Catholics view marriage as a sacrament, a sacred and lifelong bond blessed by God.

questions.q: Which 1968 papal encyclical restated the Catholic Church's opposition to artificial contraception?
questions.explain: Humanae Vitae (1968), issued by Pope Paul VI, opposed the use of artificial contraception.

questions.q: In Islam, the marriage contract is known as the...
questions.explain: The nikah is the Islamic marriage contract that formalises the union between a couple.

questions.q: "There is neither...male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus" is found in which book of the Bible?
questions.explain: This teaching from Galatians 3:28 is used to support Christian belief in the equality of men and women.

questions.q: What is the term for a married person having sex with someone who is not their spouse?
questions.explain: Adultery is a sexual relationship between a married person and someone other than their marriage partner.

questions.q: A family made up of two parents and their children living together is best described as a...
questions.explain: A nuclear family consists of two parents and their children living in one household.

questions.q: According to a hadith, which permitted action is described as the most hated by Allah?
questions.explain: A hadith teaches that of all permitted things, divorce is the most hated by Allah, though it remains allowed.

questions.q: Why does the Catholic Church not permit remarriage in church after divorce while a former spouse is alive?
options: Marriage is a lifelong sacred bond that cannot be broken
Remarriage is illegal in most countries
It believes couples should only marry once for financial reasons
questions.explain: Catholics teach marriage is a lifelong sacramental bond, so the Church does not recognise divorce as ending a valid marriage.

questions.q: Why do many Christians believe sex should take place only within marriage?
options: It expresses lifelong commitment and love between a couple
It is required by UK law
It guarantees a couple will have children
It is only for those over the age of thirty
questions.explain: Many Christians see sex as a gift from God best expressed within the committed, faithful relationship of marriage.

questions.q: What does 'gender equality' mean in the context of relationships and families?
options: Men and women having equal rights, status and opportunities
Men always being the head of the household
Women taking sole responsibility for childcare
Only men being allowed to work outside the home
questions.explain: Gender equality means men and women should be treated as equal in rights, status and opportunities.

questions.q: Which teaching best supports the Christian belief that marriage should be lifelong?
options: "What God has joined together, let no one separate"
"Do not store up treasures on earth"
questions.explain: Jesus' teaching that no one should separate what God has joined is used to support lifelong marriage.

questions.q: Why does the Catholic Church accept Natural Family Planning but reject artificial contraception?
options: It does not use artificial means and works with the body's natural cycle
It is cheaper than other methods
It guarantees a couple will never have children
It was recommended by the government
questions.explain: Natural Family Planning is accepted because it avoids artificial interference with the natural reproductive process.

questions.q: Why do some Christians support more traditional gender roles within the family?
options: They follow teachings about the husband as the head of the family
They believe women should never marry
They reject the idea of having children
They think men should not work
questions.explain: Some Christians base traditional roles on biblical teachings, such as St Paul's, describing the husband as head of the household.

questions.q: What is an annulment in the Catholic Church?
options: A declaration that a valid marriage never truly existed
A ceremony to renew marriage vows
A blessing for a second marriage
A form of religious divorce that permits remarriage freely
questions.explain: An annulment declares that a true, valid marriage never took place, rather than ending a valid marriage.

questions.q: Why do most religious believers oppose adultery?
options: It breaks the vows and trust of marriage
It is encouraged in most holy books
It is a legal requirement to avoid it
It has no effect on family life
questions.explain: Adultery is widely condemned because it breaks the promises of faithfulness and trust made in marriage.

questions.q: A Catholic whose first spouse is still alive asks their priest to be married again in church. What is the most likely response?
options: The Church would not permit a church remarriage
The Church would encourage it immediately
The Church would insist they cohabit first
The Church would require them to divorce again
questions.explain: As Catholics regard marriage as a lifelong bond, the Church would generally not remarry someone whose former spouse is alive.

questions.q: A Church of England couple wish to delay having children for a few years. Which choice would their Church accept?
options: Using contraception to plan their family
questions.explain: The Church of England accepts the responsible use of contraception to help couples plan their family.

questions.q: Two women in a committed relationship are raising a child together. Which term best describes this family?
questions.explain: A same-sex parent family is one in which children are raised by a same-sex couple.

questions.q: A father stays at home to raise the children while the mother works full time. How would a Christian who believes in gender equality most likely respond?
options: This is acceptable because roles are not fixed by gender
This is forbidden because only mothers may raise children
This is wrong because women must not work
This is only allowed if the couple divorce
questions.explain: A Christian who supports gender equality would accept that domestic and working roles need not be determined by gender.

specSource: AQA GCSE Religious Studies A specification; Theme A: Relationships & Families
